--- title: Graduation assessment — independently deliver task comments, not another tutorial description: Business requirements, constraints, negative scenarios and review criteria only; demonstrate authorization, concurrency, upgrades, rollback, recovery and invited use with independent evidence. --- import { getGraduationExample } from '@/lib/js2py-examples' ## 1. An independent delivery, not a final implementation answer Understanding a backend tutorial does not establish that you can make maintainable choices without its reference implementation. This chapter supplies no physical schema, route design, migration commands, transaction algorithm or complete backend. Extend your own collaborative task API and explain why you chose a design, how you discovered mistakes, and how you recover. The prerequisite is **O06 capability and evidence**, not an accessible lesson page. Your existing project needs isolated restoration, access control and controlled-release foundations. If a preceding chapter lacks an environment, restoration or mainline acceptance, you may prepare G01 requirements, but G01 cannot mark that prerequisite verified. Mainline review controls chapter status. Task comments are an equivalent controlled alternative to the capstone's label extension: you do not need both, and delivery gates are not relaxed. New complexity comes from distinct author/owner permissions, concurrent revisions, redaction and repeated requests, all of which must survive upgrade, release rollback and restoration. Adding another CRUD table is not sufficient. Download the [G01 requirements and evidence package](/learning-assets/js2py/g01-graduation.zip) and enter `g01-graduation`. It contains a product contract, synthetic scenario data, evidence/reviewer templates, a rubric and a **material-format checker**, not a deployable reference backend. Every student scenario starts as `not_run`; no pilot data is fabricated. ## 2. Four different claims need four different kinds of evidence | Claim | Who supplies which evidence | What cannot be inferred | | --- | --- | --- | | Course content complete | Author supplies text, resources, links and required mainline review | The learner has mastered it or every earlier environment was executed | | Author reference validation | Author actually executes owned examples/material checks in a stated environment | A student's different implementation is correct | | Student graduation | Independent project evidence, negative cases, restoration, an unseen change and human review | Unrestricted public operation is safe | | Real public operation | Identified host/domain/credential ownership, HTTPS, safe deployment, budget, monitoring and real-use evidence | Permanent safety, unlimited capacity or no maintenance obligation | The author of this chapter verified only its requirements package and format tool. Your project was not run, graduation was not awarded, and no host, domain or deployment credentials are available to prove a public release. Invited use is also different from public registration: audience, data risk and operational commitments differ. The template keeps these claims separate rather than collapsing them into `passed=true`.
Review check 1: why is a green CI screenshot insufficient for graduation? It may refer to a different revision, exercise only happy paths, bypass the real database, or run only the format checker. Review needs traceable revision, environment, input, outcome and persistent state, plus independent adaptation and restoration. A screenshot can help locate a record, but cannot replace reviewable primary evidence. Author, student and operational evidence must identify their separate provenance.
## 3. The new requirement: task comments with immutable authorship Logically a comment has identity, owning task/project, server-derived author, plain text, creation time, a revision after successful modification, and redaction state. Text contains 1–1000 Unicode code points, is not whitespace-only and cannot be NULL. Rich text, attachments, nested replies and real-time notifications are excluded. These are logical facts, not a prescribed physical table. Storage, interface representation and conflict responses are decisions you must defend. Current active project members can read/list/create and edit or redact their own visible comments. A project owner can redact any comment in that project, but **cannot rewrite another author's text**. A removed member cannot read or operate on that project's comments, even with an unexpired old credential or historical authorship. Current members still see the historical author attribution. Anonymous and disabled users receive no access merely because a membership row remains. Normal reads of a redacted comment expose tombstone metadata, not the original text. Lists, detail, history, exports and logs must not become bypasses. Editing after redaction fails; delayed requests cannot resurrect text. Choose and explain internal retention or deletion and its backup consequences. Do not claim retroactive erasure from every existing backup. {getGraduationExample('requirements.json')} This is a machine-readable product contract shared by all three editions, not database DDL. Keep product requirements separate from your implementation constraints: preventing former-member access is required; choosing a particular framework is not a scoring item. Extra microservices, public registration or a new authentication protocol cannot substitute for required evidence. ## 4. One Alice demo cannot establish data, role and failure boundaries Synthetic data includes two projects and owners, an ordinary member, a removed member, an outsider and a disabled user. The same person may remain authorized in another project. Logical IDs describe scenarios: supply a mapping into your own model rather than treating these labels as prescribed database key types, and never overwrite production users with them. {getGraduationExample('fixtures/actors-and-data.json')} Especially revealing evidence uses someone who is correctly authenticated but does not own the object: combine a foreign comment ID with an owned project path, forge an author field, or replay an old request after removal. Testing only 401 establishes a login check, not every object boundary. After rejection, verify no mutation and no text disclosure rather than checking only an HTTP status. Input boundaries need more than an empty string: Unicode whitespace, NULL, maximum length, one code point beyond the maximum, and markup characters as plain text are all part of the contract. No elaborate new frontend is required. The API and necessary display contract can express plain-text semantics without interpreting comment text as executable rich HTML. ## 5. Concurrency, repeated requests and uncertain outcomes differ Two edits based on the same old revision must not silently overwrite one another successfully. Declare conflict behavior and prove actual interleaving using independent requests. A committed redaction cannot be undone by a delayed edit. Requests beginning after membership removal commits must be denied; define and test a consistent policy for already in-flight work rather than selecting whichever run looks favorable afterward. The repeated-create contract is a retention window of at least 24 hours: the same authenticated actor, task, request identity and content represent one logical comment and return the same identity. Different text with the same scoped request identity conflicts without changing the original. Different actors or tasks must not receive each other's cached result. Choose a bounded, documented, tested expiry policy rather than promising exactly-once behavior forever. A replay must still satisfy current permission. Revocation cannot be bypassed by “this request previously succeeded.” A lost response also does not mean the database failed to commit. S16 specifically requires an accepted request whose response was not received to be retried without creating a duplicate. This is a product requirement, not an instruction to copy a particular idempotency middleware. Failure evidence identifies the stage, what should remain, what must not exist, and how a subsequent valid operation recovers. “Caught an exception” does not describe the database afterward. Final row counts alone can miss a success promised externally without a corresponding record. External outcomes and persistent state must explain each other. ## 6. The scenario catalog is an acceptance contract, not a ready-made suite Twenty-four scenarios cover functionality, object authorization, concurrency, repeated requests, failures, queries, upgrade, rollback, recovery, operations, pilot use and independent ability. They contain no request implementation or database answer. Build reproducible evidence against your own interface contract. {getGraduationExample('scenarios.json')} A convincing record identifies the application/migration revision, exclusive environment, relevant actors, redacted inputs, actual responses, subsequent database/service state and how to observe it again. Concurrency evidence must demonstrate overlap rather than labeling two sequential calls a race. A scenario marked pass is your assertion, still subject to review. Fail preserves a counterexample; blocked states what is missing and who can unblock it; not_run invents neither timestamps nor output. Test count, coverage percentage and screenshot volume cannot replace decisive negative cases. Stable pagination requires deterministic results for an unchanged dataset; insertion/deletion behavior must be explained rather than equating total ordering with a cross-request snapshot.
Review check 2: two successful creates leave one row — does that prove duplicate-request correctness? Not by itself. Verify matching scope/request identity, identical returned comment identity, no overwrite by a different payload, no response reuse across users, denial after revocation, and recovery from a lost response. One final row could result from cleanup or incorrect merging. A set of evidence must explain accepted outcomes and persistent state together. No implementation algorithm is supplied here.
## 7. Upgrade, rollback and restoration must include existing data Starting on an empty database does not prove upgrade safety. Existing users, projects, members and tasks retain their identities and permitted behavior; old tasks begin with zero comments, without invented default authors. A task with any comment, including a tombstone, cannot be physically deleted. Deletion of uncommented tasks retains its previous behavior. Project deletion must not bypass this rule; document and test a consistent project policy. Rollback evidence must identify which application revision is compatible with which schema revision. If an old application cannot understand new state, a declared safe freeze or controlled rollback condition is acceptable, but blindly downgrading and losing accepted comments is not successful recovery. Test compatibility and preservation against meaningful data, not an empty demonstration database. Restoration requires actually restoring a backup into a different, explicitly isolated target. Check relationships, revisions, redaction privacy and repeated-request behavior, and record recovery duration and acceptable/observed loss windows. Table counts can miss resurrected redacted text or missing replay state. An older backup can contain old content; explain retention and the restored data window rather than treating backups as merely a performance concern. Without an approved target, account, budget and O06 evidence, pilot use remains blocked. Once those conditions are met, limit it to 2–5 invited testers with nonsensitive data and at least one traceable anonymized feedback item followed by a verified adjustment. Never invent participants or describe a localhost URL as public HTTPS. ## 8. A rubric needs gates: attractive documentation cannot offset unauthorized access {getGraduationExample('rubric.json')} Six dimensions total 100 points, with a suggested minimum of 80. All 24 scenarios describe required behavior and need reviewed passing evidence; a false hard_gate flag is not a waiver. Hard-gate failures cannot be offset by points, and O06 must be independently confirmed. Unauthorized access, data loss, fabricated evidence, exposed credentials and inability to explain an independent change cannot be offset by a polished UI or higher coverage. The rubric is not an automatic graduation engine; a human reviewer owns the decision. Official documentation and assistance tools are allowed, with disclosure of assisted work. An unseen assessment change might tighten the limit for new comments while retaining readability of older long comments. Review concerns whether you can identify affected contracts, adjust validation and explain compatibility, not how much code you can type under pressure. Also defend a real problem you encountered: initial hypothesis, counterevidence, diagnostic material, repair result and remaining limits. Reciting someone else's conclusion is insufficient.
Review check 3: does a successful restore and score above 80 permit immediate public registration? No. Restoration may satisfy a graduation gate, but public operation brings audience, abuse, quotas, account recovery, budget and ongoing ownership obligations. This course's first scope is approved invited use. Graduation still leaves declared capacity and risk limits in place. Without host/domain/credentials and actual deployment evidence, record not run or blocked; the author cannot fill in “deployed” for you.
## 9. The format checker deliberately cannot graduate you The package has no external Python dependencies and needs no pytest, database, Docker or frontend build. Its optional checker uses the standard library and was tested with Python **3.13.15**. Reading JSON/Markdown does not require installing Python at all. Execute these commands inside the package, first checking the active interpreter. ```bash python3 --version python3 check_evidence.py templates/evidence.json python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -v ``` ```text {"artifact_files_verified": false, "backend_verified": false, "format_valid": true, "graduation_awarded": false, "public_operation_verified": false, "scenario_status_counts": {"blocked": 0, "fail": 0, "not_run": 24, "pass": 0}} ``` Exit 0 means the materials have an acceptable format: complete scenario IDs, separate claims, syntactically complete references, nonescaping paths and parseable fields such as times. It **does not open artifacts to verify hashes, authenticate claims, call a backend, scan every secret, award a score or confirm deployment**. A unit test deliberately constructs an in-memory fictional report that passes format checks while backend_verified stays false. That limitation test is not fabricated deployment evidence. The author ran 15 material unit tests: blank template, missing scenarios, duplicate IDs, pass without references, unsafe paths, false timestamps, blocked without a reason, dangling synthetic references and malformed JSON, among others. None of the student's 24 business scenarios was run. Do not combine those counts into “39 passing backend tests.” ## 10. Pause around evidence, without prescribing implementation order You can pause at requirements understanding, design review, behavior observation, delivery/recovery evidence or independent defense. These are evidence-maturity states, not an instruction to create one table before a particular endpoint. Choose your development order, provided every commitment is eventually reviewable. {getGraduationExample('templates/checkpoint.json')} At each pause record code/schema revisions, the owned target, last actual command, last established fact, unresolved questions, next evidence to collect and stopped resources. On resumption, confirm that reality still matches the record. “It probably passed last time” is not a checkpoint. Missing environments remain blocked with an owner; unexecuted scenarios remain not_run rather than receiving expected success values. Relative artifact paths and digests help reviewers locate evidence, but redact first. Do not share full environment dumps, tokens, connection passwords, real private comment text or private keys. Correlation IDs should help reconstruct incidents, not create another disclosure channel. The format checker is not a confidentiality audit; the submitter still reviews shared material manually. ## 11. Delivery boundary and necessary references The student's deliverable is their own model/API decisions, reviewed migrations, implementation and regression tests, failure/concurrency records, release rollback and isolated restoration, invited feedback, operating costs/limits and independent diagnosis. The download only expresses these requirements; it does not supply those outcomes. Content completion, author material validation, student graduation and real public operation remain separately assessed claims. Verified **2026-09-28**. Only necessary official references clarify existing acceptance boundaries; they do not introduce a new architecture: - [OWASP API1 object-level authorization](https://owasp.org/API-Security/editions/2023/en/0xa1-broken-object-level-authorization/): authentication alone does not establish permission for a particular object. - [PostgreSQL 18 SQL dump and restoration](https://www.postgresql.org/docs/18/backup-dump.html): producing a backup differs from performing and verifying restoration; this chapter supplies no restoration implementation steps. - [Idempotent methods in HTTP semantics](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9110.html#name-idempotent-methods): repeated-request effects relate to method semantics; naming a comment-creation request POST does not automatically provide the product's deduplication contract. Not completed or claimed: a student backend, execution of student business scenarios, substituted O06 acceptance, graduation assessment, real invited use, public deployment or long-term operation. The inspectable artifact here is the requirements/material tooling; other statuses require actual evidence and mainline review.

# G01 — Independent task-comment requirements and evidence package

Verified 2026-09-28. This is not a reference backend or a suite that validates a student's application. Mainline/human review must establish O06 restoration and controlled-release evidence; missing prerequisites cannot be automatically marked passed here.

## What is delivered

Task comments are an equivalent controlled alternative to the capstone label extension; both are not required. New complexity includes author versus owner permissions, membership removal, versioned editing, nonresurrectable redaction, repeated/uncertain requests, populated upgrades, rollback, restoration and invited feedback. Students choose and defend their model, interface, transaction mechanism, migrations and delivery strategy. Their implementation answers are not supplied.

- requirements.json: machine-readable product contract g01-comments-v1; logical facts are not prescribed physical tables.
- fixtures/actors-and-data.json: synthetic actors, objects and content boundaries; labels are not prescribed IDs or a production import.
- scenarios.json: S01–S24 preconditions/actions/outcomes and hard gates, not an executed backend test suite.
- rubric.json: six human-reviewed dimensions totaling 100, suggested minimum 80, and noncompensable gates.
- templates/evidence.json: unfilled student report with 24 not_run cases and four separate claims.
- templates/fixture-bindings.json: mappings into a student's isolated model, without credentials.
- templates/checkpoint.json: revisions, owned target, established facts, next evidence and stopped resources.
- templates/reviewer-record.json: blank human review without a prefilled graduation or public-operation approval.
- check_evidence.py: optional standard-library-only material-format checker.
- tests/test_materials.py: material/catalog unit tests, not comment API tests.
- sources.json, three READMEs and FILES.json: provenance, execution contract and packaging allowlist.

## Check the package without a backend, but do not infer graduation

Reading JSON/Markdown requires no runtime. Optional tools were tested on Python 3.13.15, recorded in .python-version. There are no external dependencies, so no invented dependency lock and no requirement for uv, pytest, PostgreSQL, Docker or frontend tooling. Use existing Python; install no system service.

Work inside extracted g01-graduation:

```bash
python3 --version
python3 check_evidence.py templates/evidence.json
python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -v
```

Deterministic output for the untouched template:

```text
{"artifact_files_verified": false, "backend_verified": false, "format_valid": true, "graduation_awarded": false, "public_operation_verified": false, "scenario_status_counts": {"blocked": 0, "fail": 0, "not_run": 24, "pass": 0}}
```

Expect 15 material unit tests, with variable duration. Author verification also runs them from an allowlisted ZIP extraction. They cover missing/duplicate cases, invalid references/paths, false timestamps, malformed JSON and synthetic relationships, not a student's backend. All 24 student business scenarios remain not_run.

Exit 0 means acceptable format; invalid material exits 1. The checker does not open artifact files to verify digests, authenticate claims, contact networks/databases, scan all secrets, score work, award graduation or confirm deployment. An in-memory fictional-report test deliberately proves that correct form does not establish a correct backend; it is not an operational record.

## Express evidence without prescribing implementation

Keep the original template blank and put a personal report in a separate submission directory. Executed claims should link code/schema revision, exclusive environment, time, input, response, persistent state and redacted artifact paths. Pass is the submitter's assertion subject to review; fail preserves counterexamples; blocked identifies missing conditions and ownership; not_run must not invent success or timestamps.

Concurrency requires actual overlap. A lost response cannot be replaced by assuming no commit. Recovery means actual restoration into an isolated target. A backup file, empty-database migration, green screenshot, coverage percentage or single final row can each be insufficient. The lesson's three collapsed review sections explain these counterexamples without supplying backend implementation steps.

Relative paths and sha256 fields help locate material, but the format tool does not inspect their content. The submitter checks integrity, redaction and reproducibility. Exclude tokens, passwords, private keys, full environment dumps and real private text. Without approved host/domain/budget/credentials, do not claim public deployment. Invited use also waits for its prerequisites.

## Pause and resume

Checkpoints describe evidence maturity, not a table-before-route recipe. Record actual revisions, last command, established facts, unresolved questions, next evidence and resources you stopped. On resumption compare reality to the record; do not assume previous results still hold. This package starts no services, creates no accounts and changes no database, so its checker has no cluster cleanup obligation.

Unreviewed O06 or unavailable pilot infrastructure stays blocked. This package does not change shared chapter status. Disclose assistance during independent review, explain a real diagnosis, and adapt to a reviewer-selected business change.

## Four claims and known limits

Content completion, author reference validation, student graduation and real public operation stay separate. This package proves only execution of its material tooling, not a student's graduation. Human review needs O06, the required behavior of all 24 scenarios, all gates, the rubric and independent ability. Documentation polish cannot offset unauthorized access, and a script cannot approve graduation.

No student app, migration, authorization, concurrency behavior, release/rollback, database restore or actual pilot was run. There is no public deployment or operation evidence. The tool is not a confidentiality audit, security certification or legal compliance certification. Missing earlier-chapter evidence cannot be upgraded here.

## Sources and packaging

Necessary official sources checked 2026-09-28 are recorded in sources.json: OWASP API1 object authorization, PostgreSQL 18 SQL dump/restoration and RFC 9110 idempotent methods. They clarify acceptance boundaries, not additional implementation requirements.

FILES.json matches the repository sibling g01-graduation-files.json as a per-file allowlist. The ZIP contains requirements, synthetic data, templates, tools and documentation, not submission data, caches, credentials or database storage. Mainline owns registration of canonical loader getGraduationExample, navigation/status and /learning-assets/js2py/g01-graduation.zip. This package edits no shared registry.

# G01 — 独立任务评论需求与证据包

核验日期：2026-09-28。本包不是后端参考实现，也不是可以替学生项目执行验收的测试套件。前置 O06 的恢复与受控发布证据必须由主线/评阅者核实；前章缺环境不能被本包自动标成通过。

## 交付是什么

任务评论是 capstone 标签扩展的等价受控变式，不要求两者同时完成。新增的实质复杂度是作者与项目 owner 的不同权限、成员撤销、版本化编辑、撤回后不可复活、重复请求和响应不明，以及已有数据升级、回退、恢复和受邀反馈。学生自行选择并论证模型、接口、事务机制、迁移和交付策略；包里没有这些实现答案。

- `requirements.json`：机器可读产品契约，版本 g01-comments-v1。逻辑事实不等于给定数据库表。
- `fixtures/actors-and-data.json`：纯合成主体和对象、内容边界；逻辑标签不是规定的实际 ID，也不是生产导入脚本。
- `scenarios.json`：S01–S24 的前提、行为与预期、硬门槛，不是已运行的自动化测试。
- `rubric.json`：人工评阅六维 100 分、参考线 80 及不能被分数抵消的门槛。
- `templates/evidence.json`：未填学生报告，24 场景均 not_run；四种完成声明分离。
- `templates/fixture-bindings.json`：把合成逻辑标签映射到学生测试模型；不要填凭证。
- `templates/checkpoint.json`：中断时的版本、独占目标、已证实事实、下一份证据与资源停止记录。
- `templates/reviewer-record.json`：未填的人工评阅记录；不预填毕业或公网批准。
- `check_evidence.py`：可选的材料格式检查器，仅标准库。
- `tests/test_materials.py`：格式/目录数据的单元测试，不是评论 API 测试。
- `sources.json`、三语 README、`FILES.json`：来源、运行约定和打包 allowlist。

## 不运行后端也能检查包，但不能据此毕业

只阅读 JSON/Markdown 无须任何运行环境。若要运行可选工具，本次实测 Python 3.13.15，`.python-version` 记录该基线；没有外部依赖，因此不提供虚假的依赖锁，也不要求 uv、pytest、数据库、Docker 或前端软件。使用已有 Python，不安装系统服务。

工作目录是解压后的 g01-graduation：

```bash
python3 --version
python3 check_evidence.py templates/evidence.json
python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -v
```

默认模板的确定输出：

```text
{"artifact_files_verified": false, "backend_verified": false, "format_valid": true, "graduation_awarded": false, "public_operation_verified": false, "scenario_status_counts": {"blocked": 0, "fail": 0, "not_run": 24, "pass": 0}}
```

应有 15 项材料单元测试通过，耗时不固定。作者从 allowlist ZIP 解压后也会运行这些检查。它们验证缺场景、重复、非法引用/路径、虚假时间、损坏 JSON 和合成数据关联等，不验证任何学生后端。真实学生 24 场景仍为 not_run。

格式检查器返回 0 仅指格式可接受；非法材料返回 1。它不打开证据文件核对摘要，不验证材料真实，不访问网络或数据库，不扫描所有秘密，也不能宣布评分合格、毕业或部署。单元测试在内存中故意构造一份虚构报告，证明形式正确不代表后端正确；该测试不是上线记录。

## 如何表达材料，不规定如何实现系统

保留原模板作为空白基线，把自己的报告放在另一个提交目录。每条实际执行声明应能关联代码/结构版本、独占环境、时间、输入、响应、持久状态与经过脱敏的证据路径。pass 是作者声明，仍须评阅；fail 保留反例；blocked 写清外部条件与责任人；not_run 不填预期成功或伪造时间。

并发证据必须显示真实交错，响应丢失不能用“第一次没提交”替代，恢复必须是隔离目标中的真实恢复。只有备份文件、空库迁移、绿色截图、覆盖率数字或最终一行记录都可能不足。正文三处折叠核对区解释这些评阅反例，不提供后端实现步骤。

--- title: Graduation assessment — independently deliver task comments, not another tutorial description: Business requirements, constraints, negative scenarios and review criteria only; demonstrate authorization, concurrency, upgrades, rollback, recovery and invited use with independent evidence. --- import { getGraduationExample } from '@/lib/js2py-examples' ## 1. An independent delivery, not a final implementation answer Understanding a backend tutorial does not establish that you can make maintainable choices without its reference implementation. This chapter supplies no physical schema, route design, migration commands, transaction algorithm or complete backend. Extend your own collaborative task API and explain why you chose a design, how you discovered mistakes, and how you recover. The prerequisite is **O06 capability and evidence**, not an accessible lesson page. Your existing project needs isolated restoration, access control and controlled-release foundations. If a preceding chapter lacks an environment, restoration or mainline acceptance, you may prepare G01 requirements, but G01 cannot mark that prerequisite verified. Mainline review controls chapter status. Task comments are an equivalent controlled alternative to the capstone's label extension: you do not need both, and delivery gates are not relaxed. New complexity comes from distinct author/owner permissions, concurrent revisions, redaction and repeated requests, all of which must survive upgrade, release rollback and restoration. Adding another CRUD table is not sufficient. Download the [G01 requirements and evidence package](/learning-assets/js2py/g01-graduation.zip) and enter `g01-graduation`. It contains a product contract, synthetic scenario data, evidence/reviewer templates, a rubric and a **material-format checker**, not a deployable reference backend. Every student scenario starts as `not_run`; no pilot data is fabricated. ## 2. Four different claims need four different kinds of evidence | Claim | Who supplies which evidence | What cannot be inferred | | --- | --- | --- | | Course content complete | Author supplies text, resources, links and required mainline review | The learner has mastered it or every earlier environment was executed | | Author reference validation | Author actually executes owned examples/material checks in a stated environment | A student's different implementation is correct | | Student graduation | Independent project evidence, negative cases, restoration, an unseen change and human review | Unrestricted public operation is safe | | Real public operation | Identified host/domain/credential ownership, HTTPS, safe deployment, budget, monitoring and real-use evidence | Permanent safety, unlimited capacity or no maintenance obligation | The author of this chapter verified only its requirements package and format tool. Your project was not run, graduation was not awarded, and no host, domain or deployment credentials are available to prove a public release. Invited use is also different from public registration: audience, data risk and operational commitments differ. The template keeps these claims separate rather than collapsing them into `passed=true`.
Review check 1: why is a green CI screenshot insufficient for graduation? It may refer to a different revision, exercise only happy paths, bypass the real database, or run only the format checker. Review needs traceable revision, environment, input, outcome and persistent state, plus independent adaptation and restoration. A screenshot can help locate a record, but cannot replace reviewable primary evidence. Author, student and operational evidence must identify their separate provenance.
## 3. The new requirement: task comments with immutable authorship Logically a comment has identity, owning task/project, server-derived author, plain text, creation time, a revision after successful modification, and redaction state. Text contains 1–1000 Unicode code points, is not whitespace-only and cannot be NULL. Rich text, attachments, nested replies and real-time notifications are excluded. These are logical facts, not a prescribed physical table. Storage, interface representation and conflict responses are decisions you must defend. Current active project members can read/list/create and edit or redact their own visible comments. A project owner can redact any comment in that project, but **cannot rewrite another author's text**. A removed member cannot read or operate on that project's comments, even with an unexpired old credential or historical authorship. Current members still see the historical author attribution. Anonymous and disabled users receive no access merely because a membership row remains. Normal reads of a redacted comment expose tombstone metadata, not the original text. Lists, detail, history, exports and logs must not become bypasses. Editing after redaction fails; delayed requests cannot resurrect text. Choose and explain internal retention or deletion and its backup consequences. Do not claim retroactive erasure from every existing backup. {getGraduationExample('requirements.json')} This is a machine-readable product contract shared by all three editions, not database DDL. Keep product requirements separate from your implementation constraints: preventing former-member access is required; choosing a particular framework is not a scoring item. Extra microservices, public registration or a new authentication protocol cannot substitute for required evidence. ## 4. One Alice demo cannot establish data, role and failure boundaries Synthetic data includes two projects and owners, an ordinary member, a removed member, an outsider and a disabled user. The same person may remain authorized in another project. Logical IDs describe scenarios: supply a mapping into your own model rather than treating these labels as prescribed database key types, and never overwrite production users with them. {getGraduationExample('fixtures/actors-and-data.json')} Especially revealing evidence uses someone who is correctly authenticated but does not own the object: combine a foreign comment ID with an owned project path, forge an author field, or replay an old request after removal. Testing only 401 establishes a login check, not every object boundary. After rejection, verify no mutation and no text disclosure rather than checking only an HTTP status. Input boundaries need more than an empty string: Unicode whitespace, NULL, maximum length, one code point beyond the maximum, and markup characters as plain text are all part of the contract. No elaborate new frontend is required. The API and necessary display contract can express plain-text semantics without interpreting comment text as executable rich HTML. ## 5. Concurrency, repeated requests and uncertain outcomes differ Two edits based on the same old revision must not silently overwrite one another successfully. Declare conflict behavior and prove actual interleaving using independent requests. A committed redaction cannot be undone by a delayed edit. Requests beginning after membership removal commits must be denied; define and test a consistent policy for already in-flight work rather than selecting whichever run looks favorable afterward. The repeated-create contract is a retention window of at least 24 hours: the same authenticated actor, task, request identity and content represent one logical comment and return the same identity. Different text with the same scoped request identity conflicts without changing the original. Different actors or tasks must not receive each other's cached result. Choose a bounded, documented, tested expiry policy rather than promising exactly-once behavior forever. A replay must still satisfy current permission. Revocation cannot be bypassed by “this request previously succeeded.” A lost response also does not mean the database failed to commit. S16 specifically requires an accepted request whose response was not received to be retried without creating a duplicate. This is a product requirement, not an instruction to copy a particular idempotency middleware. Failure evidence identifies the stage, what should remain, what must not exist, and how a subsequent valid operation recovers. “Caught an exception” does not describe the database afterward. Final row counts alone can miss a success promised externally without a corresponding record. External outcomes and persistent state must explain each other. ## 6. The scenario catalog is an acceptance contract, not a ready-made suite Twenty-four scenarios cover functionality, object authorization, concurrency, repeated requests, failures, queries, upgrade, rollback, recovery, operations, pilot use and independent ability. They contain no request implementation or database answer. Build reproducible evidence against your own interface contract. {getGraduationExample('scenarios.json')} A convincing record identifies the application/migration revision, exclusive environment, relevant actors, redacted inputs, actual responses, subsequent database/service state and how to observe it again. Concurrency evidence must demonstrate overlap rather than labeling two sequential calls a race. A scenario marked pass is your assertion, still subject to review. Fail preserves a counterexample; blocked states what is missing and who can unblock it; not_run invents neither timestamps nor output. Test count, coverage percentage and screenshot volume cannot replace decisive negative cases. Stable pagination requires deterministic results for an unchanged dataset; insertion/deletion behavior must be explained rather than equating total ordering with a cross-request snapshot.
Review check 2: two successful creates leave one row — does that prove duplicate-request correctness? Not by itself. Verify matching scope/request identity, identical returned comment identity, no overwrite by a different payload, no response reuse across users, denial after revocation, and recovery from a lost response. One final row could result from cleanup or incorrect merging. A set of evidence must explain accepted outcomes and persistent state together. No implementation algorithm is supplied here.
## 7. Upgrade, rollback and restoration must include existing data Starting on an empty database does not prove upgrade safety. Existing users, projects, members and tasks retain their identities and permitted behavior; old tasks begin with zero comments, without invented default authors. A task with any comment, including a tombstone, cannot be physically deleted. Deletion of uncommented tasks retains its previous behavior. Project deletion must not bypass this rule; document and test a consistent project policy. Rollback evidence must identify which application revision is compatible with which schema revision. If an old application cannot understand new state, a declared safe freeze or controlled rollback condition is acceptable, but blindly downgrading and losing accepted comments is not successful recovery. Test compatibility and preservation against meaningful data, not an empty demonstration database. Restoration requires actually restoring a backup into a different, explicitly isolated target. Check relationships, revisions, redaction privacy and repeated-request behavior, and record recovery duration and acceptable/observed loss windows. Table counts can miss resurrected redacted text or missing replay state. An older backup can contain old content; explain retention and the restored data window rather than treating backups as merely a performance concern. Without an approved target, account, budget and O06 evidence, pilot use remains blocked. Once those conditions are met, limit it to 2–5 invited testers with nonsensitive data and at least one traceable anonymized feedback item followed by a verified adjustment. Never invent participants or describe a localhost URL as public HTTPS. ## 8. A rubric needs gates: attractive documentation cannot offset unauthorized access {getGraduationExample('rubric.json')} Six dimensions total 100 points, with a suggested minimum of 80. All 24 scenarios describe required behavior and need reviewed passing evidence; a false hard_gate flag is not a waiver. Hard-gate failures cannot be offset by points, and O06 must be independently confirmed. Unauthorized access, data loss, fabricated evidence, exposed credentials and inability to explain an independent change cannot be offset by a polished UI or higher coverage. The rubric is not an automatic graduation engine; a human reviewer owns the decision. Official documentation and assistance tools are allowed, with disclosure of assisted work. An unseen assessment change might tighten the limit for new comments while retaining readability of older long comments. Review concerns whether you can identify affected contracts, adjust validation and explain compatibility, not how much code you can type under pressure. Also defend a real problem you encountered: initial hypothesis, counterevidence, diagnostic material, repair result and remaining limits. Reciting someone else's conclusion is insufficient.
Review check 3: does a successful restore and score above 80 permit immediate public registration? No. Restoration may satisfy a graduation gate, but public operation brings audience, abuse, quotas, account recovery, budget and ongoing ownership obligations. This course's first scope is approved invited use. Graduation still leaves declared capacity and risk limits in place. Without host/domain/credentials and actual deployment evidence, record not run or blocked; the author cannot fill in “deployed” for you.
## 9. The format checker deliberately cannot graduate you The package has no external Python dependencies and needs no pytest, database, Docker or frontend build. Its optional checker uses the standard library and was tested with Python **3.13.15**. Reading JSON/Markdown does not require installing Python at all. Execute these commands inside the package, first checking the active interpreter. ```bash python3 --version python3 check_evidence.py templates/evidence.json python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -v ``` ```text {"artifact_files_verified": false, "backend_verified": false, "format_valid": true, "graduation_awarded": false, "public_operation_verified": false, "scenario_status_counts": {"blocked": 0, "fail": 0, "not_run": 24, "pass": 0}} ``` Exit 0 means the materials have an acceptable format: complete scenario IDs, separate claims, syntactically complete references, nonescaping paths and parseable fields such as times. It **does not open artifacts to verify hashes, authenticate claims, call a backend, scan every secret, award a score or confirm deployment**. A unit test deliberately constructs an in-memory fictional report that passes format checks while backend_verified stays false. That limitation test is not fabricated deployment evidence. The author ran 15 material unit tests: blank template, missing scenarios, duplicate IDs, pass without references, unsafe paths, false timestamps, blocked without a reason, dangling synthetic references and malformed JSON, among others. None of the student's 24 business scenarios was run. Do not combine those counts into “39 passing backend tests.” ## 10. Pause around evidence, without prescribing implementation order You can pause at requirements understanding, design review, behavior observation, delivery/recovery evidence or independent defense. These are evidence-maturity states, not an instruction to create one table before a particular endpoint. Choose your development order, provided every commitment is eventually reviewable. {getGraduationExample('templates/checkpoint.json')} At each pause record code/schema revisions, the owned target, last actual command, last established fact, unresolved questions, next evidence to collect and stopped resources. On resumption, confirm that reality still matches the record. “It probably passed last time” is not a checkpoint. Missing environments remain blocked with an owner; unexecuted scenarios remain not_run rather than receiving expected success values. Relative artifact paths and digests help reviewers locate evidence, but redact first. Do not share full environment dumps, tokens, connection passwords, real private comment text or private keys. Correlation IDs should help reconstruct incidents, not create another disclosure channel. The format checker is not a confidentiality audit; the submitter still reviews shared material manually. ## 11. Delivery boundary and necessary references The student's deliverable is their own model/API decisions, reviewed migrations, implementation and regression tests, failure/concurrency records, release rollback and isolated restoration, invited feedback, operating costs/limits and independent diagnosis. """Unit tests for fictional materials only; never an application acceptance suite."""
import copy
import json
from pathlib import Path
import shutil
import subprocess
import sys
import tempfile
import unittest

from check_evidence import BASE, FormatError, check_catalog, read_json, validate


class MaterialFormatTests(unittest.TestCase):
    def setUp(self):
        self.data = read_json(BASE / "templates/evidence.json")
        self.ids = check_catalog()

    def test_unrun_template_is_valid_without_graduation(self):
        result = validate(self.data, self.ids)
        self.assertEqual(result["scenario_status_counts"]["not_run"], 24)
        for flag in ["backend_verified", "graduation_awarded", "public_operation_verified", "artifact_files_verified"]:
            self.assertFalse(result[flag])

    def test_four_claims_cannot_collapse_into_one(self):
        del self.data["claims"]["public_operation"]
        with self.assertRaises(FormatError): validate(self.data, self.ids)

    def test_missing_case(self):
        self.data["scenarios"].pop()
        with self.assertRaises(FormatError): validate(self.data, self.ids)

    def test_duplicate_case(self):
        self.data["scenarios"][-1] = copy.deepcopy(self.data["scenarios"][0])
        with self.assertRaises(FormatError): validate(self.data, self.ids)

    def test_pass_without_reference(self):
        self.data["scenarios"][0]["status"] = "pass"
        with self.assertRaises(FormatError): validate(self.data, self.ids)

    def test_unknown_reference(self):
        self.data["scenarios"][0]["evidence_refs"] = ["missing"]
        with self.assertRaises(FormatError): validate(self.data, self.ids)

    def test_blocked_requires_reason_not_fake_execution(self):
        case = self.data["scenarios"][0]
        case["status"] = "blocked"
        with self.assertRaises(FormatError): validate(self.data, self.ids)
        case["notes"] = "No approved deployment target."
        self.assertTrue(validate(self.data, self.ids)["format_valid"])

    def test_no_observation_time_for_not_run(self):
        self.data["scenarios"][0]["observed_at"] = "2026-09-28T09:00:00+00:00"
        with self.assertRaises(FormatError): validate(self.data, self.ids)

    def test_bool_is_not_version(self):
        self.data["schema_version"] = True
        with self.assertRaises(FormatError): validate(self.data, self.ids)

    def test_path_traversal_absolute_and_url_rejected(self):
        for path in ["../secret.txt", "/private/secret.txt", "https://example.invalid/log", "..\\secret.txt"]:
            with self.subTest(path=path):
                self.data["artifacts"] = [{"id":"a","path":path,"sha256":"0"*64,"description":"Fictional fixture"}]
                with self.assertRaises(FormatError): validate(self.data, self.ids)

    def test_fiction_can_pass_format_but_never_verify_backend(self):
        # Intentionally fictional IN MEMORY: this is the checker's limitation test,
        # not a saved successful student run or evidence that a log exists.
        self.data["project_revision"] = "fictional-unit-test-revision"
        self.data["environment"] = {"label":"fiction","isolation":"fiction","baseline":None}
        self.data["artifacts"] = [{"id":"fiction","path":"fiction/not-a-real-log.txt","sha256":"0"*64,"description":"Does not exist"}]
        case = self.data["scenarios"][0]
        case.update(status="pass", observed_at="2026-09-28T09:00:00+00:00", evidence_refs=["fiction"])
        result = validate(self.data, self.ids)
        self.assertTrue(result["format_valid"])
        self.assertFalse(result["artifact_files_verified"])
        self.assertFalse(result["backend_verified"])
        self.assertFalse(result["graduation_awarded"])
        case["observed_at"] = "2026-09-28T09:00:00"
        with self.assertRaises(FormatError): validate(self.data, self.ids)

    def test_recovery_measurements_cannot_be_negative(self):
        self.data["operations"]["measured_rto_seconds"] = -1
        with self.assertRaises(FormatError): validate(self.data, self.ids)

    def test_pilot_claim_count_boundary(self):
        self.data["operations"].update(pilot_status="pass", invited_testers=0)
        with self.assertRaises(FormatError): validate(self.data, self.ids)

    def test_catalog_dangling_fixture(self):
        with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as directory:
            dest = Path(directory) / "materials"
            for name in ["requirements.json", "scenarios.json", "rubric.json", "fixtures/actors-and-data.json"]:
                target = dest / name
                target.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
                shutil.copyfile(BASE / name, target)
            fixtures = read_json(dest / "fixtures/actors-and-data.json")
            fixtures["comments"][0]["task"] = "missing"
            (dest / "fixtures/actors-and-data.json").write_text(json.dumps(fixtures))
            with self.assertRaises(FormatError): check_catalog(dest)

    def test_cli_malformed_and_empty_data_fail_cleanly(self):
        with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as directory:
            path = Path(directory) / "invalid.json"
            for body in ["{", "{}", "null", '{"schema_version": NaN}']:
                with self.subTest(body=body):
                    path.write_text(body)
                    result = subprocess.run([sys.executable, str(BASE / "check_evidence.py"), str(path)], capture_output=True, text=True)
                    self.assertEqual(result.returncode, 1)
                    self.assertFalse(json.loads(result.stdout)["format_valid"])
                    self.assertNotIn("Traceback", result.stderr)
